data.paper_title: Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and Momentum
data.selected_experiment: Table 2, Panel A: sequential double-sorts on PRET quintiles, then ID quintiles; six-month post-formation momentum returns (winners minus losers) per ID quintile, post-1927 sample

economic_rationale.value: Frog-in-the-pan (limited attention): investors are inattentive to information arriving continuously in small amounts and process it with a delay, so momentum is stronger and more persistent after continuous information than after discrete information with similar cumulative formation-period returns.

evidence.quote: Speciﬁcally, the FIP hypothesis predicts that investors process continuous information with a delay.

universe_and_filters.value: CRSP stocks (returns adjusted for delistings), 1927 to 2007 sample; $5 price filter imposed at the beginning of each month. Share-code, exchange, and breakpoint-universe filters not stated; the data section also says negative book values are eliminated from the sample.

evidence.quote: after imposing a $5 price ﬁlter at the beginning of each month, we sort stocks

value: monthly stock returns (formation-period and holding-period returns)

evidence.quote: We obtain return data from the Center for Research in Security Prices

signal_formula_words.value: Information discreteness (ID): the sign of the formation-period cumulative return (PRET) times the percentage of formation-period days with negative daily returns minus the percentage with positive daily returns. Daily return signs are equally weighted, ignoring magnitude. Small (low) ID = continuous information; large (high) ID = discrete information. Stocks are first sorted on PRET, then on ID.

evidence.quote: Our benchmark ID proxy is determined by the sign of daily returns and ignores their magnitude by equally weighting each observed return.

signal_formula_symbols.value: ID = sgn(PRET) × [%neg − %pos]; sgn(PRET) = +1 when PRET > 0 and −1 when PRET < 0

formation_window.value: 12 months: PRET is the cumulative return over the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month; ID uses the daily returns of the same formation period

evidence.quote: PRET is deﬁned as a ﬁrm’s cumulative return over the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month.

skip_window.value: 1 month (one intermediate month between formation and holding periods)

evidence.quote: are reported for each ID quintile after skipping one intermediate month.
Post-formation returns over the next six months and three years are then computed.

rebalance_frequency.value: monthly (portfolios formed each month; handling of overlapping six-month holding periods not stated)

evidence.quote: holding-period returns in a single month after portfolio formation, with the month of portfolio formation varying across the sample period.

sort_rule_evidence.quote: into quintiles according to their PRET and then subdivide these quintiles into ID

breakpoints.value: Sequential 5x5 double sort: PRET quintiles first, then ID quintiles within each PRET quintile; breakpoint universe (NYSE vs all stocks) not stated

evidence.quote: The results in Panel A pertain to sequential double-sorts involving PRET quintiles, then ID quintiles.

favored_group.value: past winners (highest PRET quintile) in the lowest-ID (continuous information) subportfolio

evidence.quote: returns from an enhanced momentum strategy that buys past winners and sells past losers following continuous information.

disfavored_group.value: past losers (lowest PRET quintile) in the lowest-ID (continuous information) subportfolio

evidence.quote: Panel A of Table2 reports that momentum, the six-month return from buying winners and selling losers, decreases monotonically from 5.94% in the low ID quintile containing stocks with continuous information to –2.07% in the high ID quintile containing stocks with discrete information.

weighting_evidence.quote: Post-formation returns over the next six months and three years are then computed.

expected_sign_evidence.quote: Consistent with the FIP hypothesis, continuous information induces stronger and more persistent return continuation than discrete information after conditioning on the magnitude of formation-period returns.

headline_result.value: Six-month momentum (winners minus losers) is 5.94% (t = 4.63) in the continuous-information (low ID) quintile versus –2.07% in the discrete (high ID) quintile; the 8.01% difference has a t-statistic of 8.54 (post-1927).

evidence.quote: This 8.01% difference in momentum has a t-statistic of 8.54 during the post-1927 sample period.

unresolved_details: Portfolio weighting (equal vs value) of stocks within the PRET/ID subportfolios is not stated; weighting recorded as 'other' (not stated).
Whether the negative-book-value elimination stated in the data section applies to the 1927-2007 Table 2 sample is not stated.

Exact month indexing of the formation window is ambiguous: PRET is 'the past twelve months after skipping the most recent month', Table 1 says ID is computed over months t to t-11, and a separate one-month interval precedes the holding period.
Whether the six-month holding-period returns use overlapping (Jegadeesh-Titman style) portfolios or non-overlapping formation, and how they are compounded/averaged, is not stated.
Breakpoint universe for PRET and ID quintiles (NYSE vs all stocks) is not stated.
Share-code and exchange filters are not stated.
Treatment of PRET exactly equal to zero (sgn undefined) is not stated.
Minimum number of daily return observations required to compute ID is not stated.
Return convention for delistings is described only as returns 'after adjusting for delistings'.
